chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, [from Ibn Abi Umeyr], from Hanan ibn Sadeer, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Every sin is expiated by being killed in the Way of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, except for the debt. There is no expiation for it except its payment, or the creditor fulfils it, or the one who has the right excuses it.

key_terms.الْقَتْلُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: Being killed in the Way of Allah (martyrdom)

ai.seo_question: Does martyrdom forgive all sins including debts?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify that while martyrdom in the Way of Allah expiates all minor and major sins, it does not automatically absolve financial debts (al-dayn). This distinction underscores the Shia scholarly view that debts are a right of the creature (haqq al-adami) requiring specific settlement—either through payment, creditor fulfillment, or forgiveness—before the soul can fully enter Paradise.
